messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: service=runtime-kv pool=eu-central-1 metric=p99_latency value=2600ms threshold=1500ms. Auto-page to #incidents.
lina: grabbing this, oncall here. seeing p95 ~ 350ms but p99 ~ 2.6s. streaming clients reporting intermittent stall mid-stream.
marco: check kvcache metrics please — prefill_hit_ratio trending down?
anita: yes: prefill_hit_ratio dropped 40% -> 22% in 12m. decode_hit_ratio steady at 80%. eviction spikes visible. eviction_rate spiked to 95/s. fragments_count up 3x.
lina: sounds like prefill vs decode imbalance and fragmentation. which nodes?
paul: hot nodes: eu-c-3,{node-7,node-8,node-9}. fragmentation dump queued.
ops-bot: Running diagnostic job 44211: `kvcache-dump --scope eu-central-1 --nodes node-7,node-8,node-9` ETA 60s.
marco: any live mitigations we can flip quickly?
anita: short-term options: 1) bump prefill slab share to take pressure off remaining slabs, 2) reduce prefill TTL, 3) enable prefill bypass for streaming sessions shorter than X (or longer than X) depending on pattern. Also can throttle streaming concurrency per-worker.
lina: prefer minimal risk: reduce prefill TTL, enable bypass for sessions with many prefix updates, and limit streaming concurrency. Will avoid slab resize initially to not touch allocator during high load.
paul: agreed. applying: `policyctl set prefill.ttl=50s` and `policyctl set prefill.bypass=prefix_updates>5` for pool eu-central-1. Also `runtimectl set worker.streaming.max_concurrency=6`.
ops-bot: Config change started: job 44212.
incbot: Timeline: 1779990000 alert -> 1779990065 page -> 1779990140 mitigations queued.
cs: received two support reports: one enterprise reporting 15-25s stalls, one SMB reporting partial stream hangs then reconnects. Both currently on fallback model.
marco: after TTL + bypass + concurrency, p99 dropped to ~1.2s on nodes where change applied. Some nodes still near 2s.
anita: fragmentation dump: https://s3.redwood-example/diag/1779990015-frag.tar.gz — shows many small free chunks in prefill slabs. Prefill allocation churn high due to frequent short-lived prefix entries from streaming.
lina: let's not resize slabs mid-flight; schedule offline defrag. For immediate relief, enable local compaction on least-loaded nodes and rebalance prefixes away from most fragmented nodes.
paul: starting compaction on node-9 then node-7 (staggered). `kvcache compact --node node-9 --mode aggressive`
ops-bot: compaction job 44213 started on node-9. Est 120s per node.
marco: note: previously we had a bug where compaction could block decode threads for ~200ms causing slight tail blips; enable non-blocking compaction flag.
anita: set `kvcache.compact.non_blocking=true` for compaction jobs.
lina: monitoring: after compaction p99 on node-9 -> 640ms, overall pool p99 now ~820ms. streaming partial-chunk stalls reduced by ~60%.
cs: relaying to affected customers: interim fix applied, team working on full remediation and postmortem. One customer requests status call — scheduled.
marco: remaining risk: if workload shifts again to many short prefix updates, we'll see churn repeat. Need guardrails: backpressure on clients that emit many tiny prefix updates and better sampling for prefill TTL.
anita: action items: 1) schedule full slab defrag during low-traffic window (overnight). 2) implement allocator guard: block slab resize while decode_inflight > 70%. 3) add prefill_hit_ratio alert at 50% with early warning. 4) create synthetic test that simulates heavy prefix-update streaming.
lina: I'll own 1 & 3. marco takes 2. anita will run synthetic tests and write evaluation harness.
paul: handover: I'm staying on monitoring for next 30m then handing to anita for deeper remediation.
incbot: :white_check_mark: Status update: mitigations applied, p99 improved but still above target. Severity Sev2. Next update in 15m or on major change.
ops-bot: diagnostic artifacts uploaded: https://s3.redwood-example/diag/1779990020-logs.tar.gz and compaction logs at https://s3.redwood-example/diag/1779990050-compact.log
marco: for postmortem include timeline, config changes, compaction notes, customer impact summary, and runbook improvements.
cs: customers updated. one enterprise asked for ETA on defrag; told them 8 hours for full remediation & postmortem.
lina: excellent response, thanks all. keeping thread pinned.
incbot: Incident closed? not yet — monitoring window 30m. Will auto-close if p99 < 500ms for 30m.
